messages:
anya: FWIW hitting a weird one with `redwoodctl local serve` inside Docker + WSL. It picks up my default profile locally but inside the container it keeps falling back to anonymous tokens after a few requests.

michael: ugh. do you mount ~/.redwood or set REDWOOD_CONFIG?

anya: mounting, yes. volume: "~/.redwood:/home/dev/.redwood:rw". When I switch kube contexts it works for a minute then errors like:

anya: ```
ERROR: auth: no cached credential for profile "dev"
status: 401
```

sophia: sounds like token refresh isn't happening inside the container process. redwoodctl normally spawns a refresh goroutine. are you running an old binary in the image?

anya: image built from base: debian slim + redwoodctl v0.12.2. host has v0.13.1.

michael: that explains it. v0.13 switched to a file-watcher for the config cache + a sidecar refresher, so older binaries won't see updates made by host or vice versa.

anya: oof. we can't rebuild the image on every machine. any workaround?

alex: short-term: set REDWOOD_PROFILE and REDWOOD_TOKEN env vars in the container start so the process has a static token for tests. longer-term: either upgrade binary in image or run host agent (redwood-auth-proxy) as a sidecar.

michael: example env hack:

michael: ```bash
docker run -e REDWOOD_PROFILE=dev \
  -e REDWOOD_TOKEN="$(cat ~/.redwood/cache/dev/token)" \
  -v ~/.redwood:/home/dev/.redwood:ro my-app-image
```

anya: that works for short E2E runs. but for local iterative dev the token TTL is annoying. would be great if redwoodctl had a `--force-profile` or `--no-filewatch` flag to opt into static behavior for containers.

alex: filing a wishlist item.

devex-bot: Created DE-2381 with title: "redwoodctl: explicit container-friendly profile flags (force-profile / no-filewatch)" :white_check_mark:

sophia: for reproducible localserve, also consider symlinking the host cache path into the container at the same absolute path the binary expects (/home/dev/.redwood/cache). filewatching relies on inode changes so relative mounts sometimes break it.

anya: good tip — symlink + upgrade binary did fix it for me. thanks.

michael: follow-up: we'll add a short note in the localserve docs about image binary parity and token-refresh behavior. also adding a diagnostic message in redwoodctl when cache writes are ignored.

anya: would love a small CLI command to force a refresh from inside container, e.g. `redwoodctl auth refresh --profile dev` (no interactive login).

alex: there's a prototype: `redwoodctl auth refresh --non-interactive --profile dev` in the cli-wip branch. i'll push a PR and tag you.

anya: thanks — that'd save a ton of friction when juggling contexts. :pray:
